data.long_meaning: The name Konark is derived from two Sanskrit words: Kona, meaning 'angle' or 'corner', and Arka, meaning 'sun'. The name Konark carries the meaning “Sun Temple” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Konark usually hope their child will grow to embody sun temple and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The Temple of Konark, also known as the Sun Temple, is a UNESCO World Heritage site and one of India's most famous attractions. This 13th-century temple was built to honor the sun god Surya and his chariot, and it is an exemplary representation of the Orissan architectural style. The intricate carvings and sculptures on the temple walls depict various mythological stories and celestial beings. The temple's annual chariot festival, known as the 'Chariot Festival of Konark', is a significant cultural event, attracting tourists from all corners of the world.
